title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-16
content:
Daily scratchpad - GPU ops / infra notes

2026-03-04 (wip)
- Morning stand notes: trouble with tgx-3 rack (nvlink flaps reported). Put in temporary capacity redistribution.
- Hit repeated OOMs on model-serving-prod-xx when sequence length > 4096 (batching tweak needed).

Top priorities:
1) Capacity plan Q2 (draft numbers) - finalize by Thu
   - Current reserved GPUs: 120 A100s (dedicated). Usable: ~112 after maintenance headroom.
   - Projected Q2 demand (hosted + bursts): ~150k token/s peak -> need +20% buffer -> target 140 A100-equivalent.
   - Action: run cost projection script (scripts/capacity/calc_q2_forecast.sh) and check with finance.

2) TGX-3 nvlink instability follow-up
   - Symptoms: nvlink disconnects on node tgx3-07 around 03:40 UTC for 2-3s, then reconnect. Cause unknown.
   - Checks done: driver (525.85) last updated 2026-02-18, kernel patched 5.15.88. No recent reboot.
   - TODO: schedule controlled reboot of tgx3-07 during maintenance window (Sat 03/06 02:00-04:00 UTC) if not resolved by monitoring alert.
   - Add telemetry: enable extended logs (nvlink debug) for 24h -> /var/log/nvlink-debug.log (rotate after collection).

3) Memory leak repro on model-serving-prod-12
   - Repro steps: send synthetic long-prefix loads (seq len 8192) with batch size 1, observe steady increase in GPU VRAM usage over 6h. Suspect KV cache not cleared on error path.
   - Linked ticket: JIRA-INFRA-3421 (assigned to @samir).
   - Quick workaround: reduce max_seq to 6144 for that route until fix landed. Add canary to 5% of traffic.

Operational TODOs (quick):
- [ ] Update node labels for private pool -> tag:private-vpc-1 (so router policy picks correct pool)
- [ ] Add auto-fallback policy: when dedicated pool < 10% capacity, route to hosted lightweight model (rwd-open-llama-7b-q4)
- [ ] Verify KV cache eviction intervals across all serving nodes (default: 30m) -> consider lowering for aggressive multi-tenant tests
- [ ] Patch CUDA driver on staging: 526.x -> run smoke tests (embedding & chat)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider adding proactive pre-warm on expected launch times (use time-based warmup, e.g., 5m before marketing blasts). Could save cold-start tail latencies.
- Batching policy: experiments show dynamic batching + latency SLO at 150ms p95 gives best cost/latency tradeoff. Document config in console route: /routes/longform-generate.

Commands / snippets I use often:
- Check GPU mem + processes: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.total,memory.used,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 5
- Collect dmesg nvlink: sudo dmesg | grep -i nvlink -A 30 > /tmp/nvlink-dmesg-$(date +%s).log
- Restart serving on node: sudo systemctl restart rwd-serving && journalctl -u rwd-serving -f --since "5m"

Open questions / blockers:
- Should we increase maintenance headroom to 10% (currently 6%) for TGX nodes? Tradeoff: cost vs reliability. Discuss with Priya.
- Need clarity from networking on recent BGP flap: ticket NET-298 (Samir looped). Impact on cross-rack traffic (affects sharded models).

Meeting follow-ups:
- 2026-03-05 10:30 sync with SRE + Monitoring - bring NVLink logs + alert history
- 2026-03-06 02:00 maintenance window (tentative) for controlled reboot of tgx3-07 (confirm with platform ops pager on-call)

Mini-retro (last week):
- Good: autoscaler handled 2x traffic spike on host-api last Thu with <2% error rate.
- Bad: forgot to update runbook after rolling patch - confusion during incident. Add checklist item: update runbook immediately after patch.

Random notes (brain dump):
- Investigate prometheus rule: gpu_memory_leak_rate (samples show anomalous trend for prod-12 only). Possibly mislabeling in exporter.
- PR to land: infra/monitoring #987 (increase prometheus retention for GPU metrics) - got +1 from Priya, needs final review.

End of scratchpad.

(If lost: refer to Confluence runbook linked above, and ticket JIRA-INFRA-3421 for the memory leak thread.)
